Unseating at the last when still in with every chance on debut at Downpatrick in May, The Cistercian is another for the shortlist.

The same can be said of Tango Theatre who returned to form last time in Ireland and will appreciate this quick ground. She heads the list of dangers.

The latter has been struggling of late over fences but returns hurdling off a generous mark and with a much easier lead likely here he could be tough to peg back. However the former has been thriving over the larger obstacles recently and was only undone in his hat trick bid here by an overly negative ride. If getting a stiffer test here he can take advantage of a much lower rating. Another who has shaped like a strong stayer at the trip is the unexposed Sharp Glance and she can complete the tricast.

Dream Pirate is 7 lbs higher than his last winning mark; however, he was a very decent 2nd off the mark of 66 last time at Nottingham, always keeping on in the closing stages. He can run well here and get another 2nd place finish under his name. Absolute Star is very lightly raced and could easily defy the long 212-day break; however, he might have to just settle for a place here before progressing further down the line.

Albeit he is 6 lbs higher than when he landed the race last year, he has been in decent form without winning this season; therefore, the handicapper might not have got a grip on him yet, and he could be primed and ready to win this again. Trefor is a fastly improving sort who could be too good for these; however, he might have to settle for a place off a career-high mark here. And Mon Na Slieve is another one who won well last time out but does have the 9 lb raise in the weights to deal with; he might have to settle for a place here.

selections.comment: Not the strongest of Novice contests; therefore, a chance can be taken on the well-bred GRAN DESCANS for Harry Charlton. The Frankel colt did not run as a 2yo and does look to be a big raw type; therefore, he has been given plenty of time to grow and mature. He could only manage a 9th place finish on debut and was beaten by 10 lengths; however, he was given an educational ride that day, according to connections; therefore, he will certainly come on for the run here. He is well-bred and will appreciate this slight step up in trip here. Bahadur is coming on nicely with each passing run; however, he might have to settle for another place finish behind a nicely bred rival here who could be anything. And Chico Magnifica makes his belated debut for a powerful yard; he will no doubt be primed and ready to run a huge race here.

selections.comment: HORNSEA BAY is one of two runners for David O'Meara and The Horse Watchers, and he looks to also be their first string here given the jockey booking. This will be his second run since having the wind operation; therefore, he is entitled to come on for the run last time, which wasn't too bad of a run when coming 4th in a handicap contest at Epsom last time out on probably the unsatisfactory softer ground conditions. He was a winner on racecourse debut for the team at Ayr back in September of last year, so there is clearly plenty of talent there, and he hails from a yard that knows how to get them back firing in these types of handicap contests. Las Ramblas was another one to win on debut back in February of last year; he came last of 12 last time out, but that was his first run in a while and first run since wind surgery and the gelding operation; he will come on for that run and place here. Elsass comes from a yard that is in form at present, but he might have to settle for another placed finish here.

selections.comment: ALONDRA is a previous winner over this distance, and although she is yet to win on the turf in her career, she has been really knocking on the door recently. A 3rd over this course and distance back in April, she has since come 3rd at Windsor and 2nd at Newmarket last time out, not getting beaten all that far and running well in the process. Just 2 lb's higher than her last winning mark, which was at Southwell back in early April, she has been running well lately on the turf and therefore looks primed to strike here. Miss Brazen was a nice enough winner last time out, and with the 7 lb rise in the weights to deal with here, she might have to settle for a 2nd place finish. And Thunder Star does like it at this track; however, the top weight might have to settle for filling the places here on this occasion.

He has another 1 lb raise to deal with here after that 2nd from last time, but given the form he is in at present, he can easily go in again at a venue he won at not so long ago. Ishe Worth Agamble also won over course and distance back in June, before backing that up with a placed effort at Carlisle last time; he can go well here and fill the placings.

Guernsey Lady is next on the list and she needs to bounce back having struggled at Royal Ascot in the G2 Queen Mary Stakes. She'll be much more comfortable back at this kind of level and is on a workable opening mark.  She should be in the shake-up

selections.comment: KENTUCKY RIVER has a good opportunity to open his account in a small but tight affair. Ollie Sangster's gelding was beaten around three lengths last time when upped to 1m6f with his efort petering out late. The drop back to 1m4f will help (his best effort to date was over 1m3f) and the assessor has dropped him a further 2lb. He should go close. Is I Right, the most experienced in the field along with West Tyrone, is a big danger having already won over course and distance (off 6lb lower) and looks pretty versatile ground-wise so should cope with any changes in conditions. He has to show more than last time when failing to beat a rival in a small field event at Newmarket (beaten just over 4l) but his three runs here are a cut above the rest of his form and he can be expected to lay down a stiff challenge. selections.comment: A fascinating puzzle with plenty in with a realistic shout. Sword is perhaps the most solid option having landed a class 4 handicap last time showing a bit of improvement on ninth career start. That came in a first time hood which is retained and David O'Meara's gedling is unlikely to have reached the ceiling of his ability yet. He shoud go very close but a chance is taken with another with scope for a bit more yet but at the other end of the weight scale, SOLDIERS STAR. Hugo Plamer's charge could go off at inflated odds given his chances are obscured by less than impressive recent form figures since opening his account at Kempton over 7f in March. However, there are some valid excuses (he was pestered for the lead last time and the straight track didn't suit), and his fifth on penultimate start over course and distance was a lot better than at first appears. He lead form pillar to almost post just being swamped late having tried to fend them off gamely. Dropped a pound since then he dictate in a first time visor and may just be able to fend them all off this time. Havana Prince is reliable and feared but an improved run is expected from Byzantine Empress whose two efforts over this CD rate amongst her very best and she may reward each way support

selections.comment: If turned out quickly May Call You Back is likely to prove extremely popular as he's been thriving for his new top stable and won eased down last time. However he was helped by a late faller that day and may be vulnerable to top weight BURRU here. The selection was in fine form over hurdles in the autumn with those efforts working out well and he produced an improved effort on his recent chase return where just out-battled late by a race fit rival. He appeared outstayed that day so a drop in distance at a stiff track should play to his strengths and he's entitled to come on plenty for that outing. Of the others Early Arrival holds each way appeal at big odds as although he's never been as good in this discipline he is dangerously well treated on his hurdles form.
